title: A Portrait for the Autopsy
premise: Ines Ashgrove, the concierge of the Grand Meridian Hotel, has spent two decades as the town of Hollow Creek's unofficial archivist—every affair, debt, and disappearance filed in his memory. When a nervous stranger pays a year's lodging upfront and asks Ines to prove that Councilman Elias Voss will not be murdered on the coming solstice night, Ines dismisses it as madness until he finds the man dead three days early, staged to look like the unsolved drowning from twenty years ago. Digging into the old case, Ines discovers the town's founding families covered up a death then, and now someone is executing them one by one in poetic retribution. The killer is Marta, the hotel's beloved housekeeper and Ines's closest friend, whose sister was the original victim; in the end, Ines must choose between handing her to the law he no longer trusts or helping her disappear—the way he once helped everyone else vanish.
about_author: S. M. Crane is the pen name of a former night-desk clerk at a grand seaside hotel who claims to have witnessed every sin except an honest apology. A Portrait for the Autopsy is their third novel, written entirely between the hours of midnight and dawn.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Sins
chapters.summary: Ines Ashgrove's POV. A day at the Grand Meridian concierge desk establishes his gift: he reads guests like ledgers, filing secrets by alphabet. He smooths over a councilman's indiscretion with practiced ease. Emotional beat: quiet pride in invisibility, shadowed by loneliness—he knows everyone and is known by no one.

chapters.title: A Year Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A gaunt stranger named Corwin checks in, pays twelve months upfront in cash, and asks Ines to prove that Councilman Elias Voss will not be murdered on the solstice. Ines laughs him off—but pockets the retainer. Emotional beat: intrigue piercing routine; the first crack in twenty years of neutrality.

chapters.title: Solstice Comes Early
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Three days before the solstice, Voss is found drowned in his bathtub, arranged exactly like the infamous 2004 drowning of a girl named Lily Ferris. Police call it coincidence. Ines remembers Corwin's question and feels the floor tilt. Emotional beat: dread replacing detachment.

chapters.title: What the Housekeeper Saw
chapters.summary: Marta's POV (first shift away from Ines). The hotel's warm, unflappable housekeeper cleans Voss's suite before police arrive and quietly pockets a torn photograph. She lies smoothly to Detective Rourke. Emotional beat: tenderness with an edge—Marta loves this hotel and hides something ferocious beneath her calm.

chapters.title: Closed for Good
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines visits the retired coroner, Dr. Pell, who signed off on Lily Ferris's accidental drowning in 2004. Pell is defensive, hands shaking, insisting the file is sealed. That night Pell's office burns. Emotional beat: the past isn't sleeping—it's counting down.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of the Dead
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Using his mental archive, Ines lists everyone connected to the 2004 case: four founding-family names, one coroner, one missing witness. He realizes the pattern—each death will mirror details of Lily's drowning. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt awakening after decades of dormancy.

chapters.title: Corwin's Empty Room
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Corwin vanishes, leaving behind a notebook of clippings about Lily Ferris and a note: 'I told you when. I never said I was innocent.' Ines suspects Corwin orchestrated events—or fled something worse. Emotional beat: betrayal and vertigo; his client may be the killer or the next victim.

chapters.title: Rourke's Offer
chapters.summary: Detective Rourke's POV. The detective, who grew up poor among the founding families' servants, privately suspects the 2004 verdict but needs Ines's archive. He offers uneasy alliance: information for information. Emotional beat: grudging respect between two men who both serve systems they distrust.

chapters.title: The Second Name
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Founding matriarch Odette Hale receives a white lily and a train ticket dated the solstice. Ines warns her; she slams the door, revealing she recognizes the flowers. Hours later she's found suffocated in her greenhouse, a lily in her hand. Emotional beat: guilt—his warning came too late.

chapters.title: Found Family
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Marta comforts Ines over brandy in the closed bar, sharing her invented history: no family, the hotel raised her. Their friendship deepens into chosen kinship. She asks what he'd do if justice and law pointed different directions. Emotional beat: warmth that the reader will later reread as confession.

chapters.title: Lily Ferris, Age Sixteen
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines uncovers the truth of 2004: Lily, a maid's daughter, was killed at a founding-families party; the coroner falsified the report; the witness—a young housekeeper—disappeared. Ines realizes the surviving witness had a younger sister. Emotional beat: cold fury at how power launders murder into accident.

chapters.title: The Third Name
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Judge Ambrose Crane barricades himself in the hotel, hiring Ines as protection—the ultimate irony. Ines guards him through one tense night, but Crane slips out at dawn to destroy evidence and dies on the ice of the millpond, mirroring where Lily's body was found. Emotional beat: futility; you cannot guard a guilty conscience from itself.

chapters.title: One Name Left
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Only patriarch Silas Voss—Elias's father—remains. Ines pieces together that the avenger must have hotel access, knowledge of the archive, and twenty years of patience. He begins suspecting staff, then refuses to finish the thought. Emotional beat: denial curdling into horror.

chapters.title: The Photograph
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines finds in Corwin's effects the torn photograph's other half: teenage Marta holding little Lily's hand. Corwin, it emerges, was Lily's foster brother, and hired Ines not to prevent murders but to find the witness who could finally convict Silas Voss. Emotional beat: the case reframes—Corwin wanted a witness, not a vigilante.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Linen Room
chapters.summary: Ines and Marta, dual focus. Ines confronts Marta gently; she doesn't deny it. She tells him about the night Lily died, how the families bought the town, the coroner, the judge—and how no court would ever touch Silas Voss. Emotional beat: heartbreak; everything tender between them was real and impossible.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Marta explains why she stopped after three deaths: killing couldn't bring Lily back, only expose the rot. She plans one final act—not murder, but forcing Silas Voss's confession before witnesses on the solstice, using the same stage the families used to bury the truth. Emotional beat: resolve tempered by grief.

chapters.title: Rourke Closes In
chapters.summary: Rourke's POV. Rourke matches the MO to the 2004 file and identifies Marta via the missing-witness trail. Torn—his own mother scrubbed floors for the Hales—he gives Ines until midnight before arresting her. Emotional beat: the law's dilemma embodied; procedure versus conscience.

chapters.title: The Solstice Gala
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The hotel hosts the annual founders' gala; Silas Voss accepts a lifetime achievement tribute. Ines moves through the crowd rerouting guests, unlocking doors, positioning witnesses—an invisible architect of the evening. Emotional beat: all his skills of discretion turned, for once, toward exposure.

chapters.title: Confession at the Meridian
chapters.summary: Ensemble climax. On the ballroom stage, under the chandelier, Marta triggers the sound system playing Lily's recorded testimony while Ines presents the forged-then-verified autopsy file to Rourke and the press. Cornered before the town, Silas Voss breaks and confesses. Emotional beat: catharsis—the archive becomes evidence, silence becomes speech.

chapters.title: Arrest, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Rourke must arrest Marta for three deaths despite Voss's confession. Ines uses every favor, secret, and filing trick he owns to negotiate: testimony for leniency, Corwin surrendered as accomplice-witness. Emotional beat: the cost of justice—love does not exempt anyone, including Ines.

chapters.title: What Ines Filed Away
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Months later: Voss convicted, Marta sentenced but alive, writing letters Ines keeps alphabetized. The hotel hums on; new guests bring new sins. Ines catches himself teaching a young porter to notice things. Emotional beat: bittersweet continuity—the watcher has become a keeper, not just a hider.

chapters.title: A Portrait for the Autopsy
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, coda. Ines hangs a small portrait of Lily Ferris behind the front desk, unlabeled, facing the lobby where the powerful check in. A guest asks who she is. 'Someone the town owes,' Ines says, and hands over the key. Emotional beat: quiet redemption; memory given a permanent address.
